[[Category:Experimental philosophy| ]]
'''Experimental philosophy''' combines traditional methods of philosophical inquiry, such as [[intuition]] and [[common sense]], with modern scientific experiments. It seeks to answer philosophical questions via the intuition and common sense of the participants to the experiment.<ref>{{#cite:Q1837}}</ref>

== Examples ==

For instance, to investigate whether the absence of free choice removes moral responsibility, an experimental philosopher may recruit a group of participants representative of the general population, and ask them to evaluate the moral responsibility of individuals in hypothetical scenarios where the free choice is/is not absent.<ref>{{#cite:Q1837}}</ref>
